Limits on what a run may send

Source: R/core-registry-governor.R
hr_governor.Rd

A governor holds the limits that every request a run makes is checked against before it is sent: how many calls the run may make, what it may spend, the largest output cap one request may carry, and which models it may call. gr_call(), and every reader, judge, adjudication, segmenter and embeddings request in the package, goes through the same check, so a limit holds whether or not the code that makes the call looks at it.

Usage

hr_governor(
  max_calls = gr_options("max_calls"),
  max_cost_usd = gr_options("max_cost_usd"),
  max_tokens_total = gr_options("max_tokens_total"),
  max_output_tokens = gr_options("max_output_tokens"),
  allowed_models = gr_options("allowed_models"),
  allow_unpriced = gr_options("allow_unpriced")
)

Arguments

max_calls

Most requests the run may make, cache hits and embeddings requests included. NULL or Inf for no limit.

max_cost_usd

Most the run may spend, in USD. NULL or Inf for no limit.

max_tokens_total

Most tokens the run may use, prompts, replies and embedded text together. NULL or Inf for no limit.

max_output_tokens

Largest output cap one request may be sent with. A request with a larger cap is refused, not cut down. NULL or Inf for no limit.

allowed_models

Character vector of the model ids the run may call (chat and embedding models alike), or NULL for any.

allow_unpriced

TRUE to send requests to models with no registered price under a spending limit.

Value

An object of class hr_governor: a list of the six limits.

Details

A request is checked against its worst case: the most prompt tokens it can be billed for at the model's input price, plus its output cap as sent (for a reasoning model the raised cap; see gr_call()) at the output price. The prompt is counted as the trace counts it, with the JSON schema and extra body fields the request carries, a few tokens for each message's framing, and safety_margin (see gr_options()) on top. One that would take the run past max_cost_usd is refused, so a run ends at or under the limit rather than one request over it. That bound rests on two things the governor cannot see: that a provider stops a reply at its cap (a gr_mock_client() or gr_backend_client() handler that returns more is charged for what it returned), and that the provider counts the prompt within the margin of the local tokenizer. A provider that reports more prompt tokens than that, or a tokenizer far from the provider's (the "heuristic" one, say), can leave a run a little over the limit. A run whose requests leave their output cap at the model's limit is stopped while it still has headroom that a smaller cap would have used.

A refused request is not sent and is not a call: it adds nothing to the trace's calls, steps or spend. It comes back from gr_call() as a failed gr_result with refused = TRUE and an error that names the limit, and a condition of class hr_budget_refused is signalled, which a caller can catch with withCallingHandlers() or tryCatch() to stop instead. The trace records the refusal in refusals, sets budget_stop and names the limit in stop_reason: "calls", "cost", "tokens" (the token ceiling), "output" (the per-call ceiling), "model" (not an allowed model) or "unpriced".

A text-generation model with no registered price cannot be held to a spending limit, so while max_cost_usd is a finite number a request to one is refused (a condition of class hr_unpriced_model as well as hr_budget_refused), unless allow_unpriced = TRUE. With allow_unpriced = TRUE the request is sent, the trace prices it at NA, never 0, and max_calls, max_tokens_total and the other limits still apply: max_tokens_total is the limit that bounds such a run, since the spending limit cannot. An embedding model with no price is not refused; its requests count against max_calls and add nothing to the spend, as gr_read_many() warns. gr_mock_client() makes no paid requests and is never refused as unpriced. A request a gr_cache() answers spends nothing and is checked only against max_calls, max_output_tokens and allowed_models.

max_tokens_total holds the tokens of the run: the prompt and reply tokens of every call the trace records, cache hits included, and the text sent to be embedded. A request is refused when what the run has used plus its own worst case (prompt as above, reply at its cap) would pass it.

A governor is attached to a run with gr_trace(governor = ), and then governs the requests recorded into that trace. A stage that keeps a trace of its own and folds it into the one it is given (gr_read_many(), gr_claims(), gr_outline() and gr_synthesise()) holds its requests to that trace's governor, less what the given trace has already spent and used in tokens; max_calls stays a limit per document for gr_read_many() and per stage for the others, as with the options. A trace made without one, including those the package makes for itself, reads the limits from gr_options() each time it checks, so changing an option affects runs that are already going, as it always has.

See also

gr_options() for the session defaults, gr_trace(), gr_register_model() to give a model its prices

Examples

cl <- gr_mock_client(function(m, p) "ok")
tr <- gr_trace(governor = hr_governor(max_calls = 2))
vapply(1:3, function(i) gr_call(cl, "hi", trace = tr)$ok, logical(1))
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE
tr$calls
#> [1] 2
tr$stop_reason
#> [1] "calls"

# A request whose worst case would pass the spending limit is not sent.
tr <- gr_trace(governor = hr_governor(max_cost_usd = 0.001))
res <- gr_call(cl, "hi", model = "gpt-4o", trace = tr)
res$refused
#> [1] TRUE
res$error
#> [1] "spending limit reached: the 'call' request could cost up to $0.16 (up to 13 prompt tokens, and 16384 reply tokens at its cap), and the run has spent $0 of its $0.001 limit, so it was not sent; raise gr_options(max_cost_usd =) or ask for a smaller max_output"
